# Federated identity credentials on an app and on a user-assigned managed identity: a pinned copy of Learn's samples

This folder is an unmodified copy of the Microsoft Learn source for two pages, [Configure an app to trust an external identity provider](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation-create-trust) and [Configure a user-assigned managed identity to trust an external identity provider](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation-create-trust-user-assigned-managed-identity), with the include both pages share for the federated credential rules (`includes/federated-credential-configuration-considerations.md`). They hold Microsoft's samples for creating a federated identity credential: Azure CLI `credential.json` bodies, Azure PowerShell commands, `az rest` calls to Microsoft Graph, a REST request and an ARM template for a user-assigned managed identity. They come from [MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/tree/d75a90ea1b07d0d2007cfab256c1ad02653d1e35/docs/workload-id) at commit `d75a90ea1b07d0d2007cfab256c1ad02653d1e35` (February 25, 2026), the last commit to all three files; they were unchanged at the repository's head on October 30, 2026. The repository's code license (`LICENSE-CODE`) is MIT; its documentation license (`LICENSE`) is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International.

**Why the pages, not just the samples.** The samples exist only inside these pages. Pinning the source byte for byte keeps the copy checkable against upstream. `examples/non-person-identity/tests/FederationSampleHarness.ps1` extracts the samples, unmodified, at test time: it checks the `credential.json` bodies and the ARM template's audience with the chapter's credential checks, runs the Azure PowerShell command against a stand-in, and sends the `az rest` and REST requests to NpiFederation's fake Graph and Resource Manager. Nothing is installed and nothing signs in. The [developer workbook *Building Non-Person Identity*, Chapter 05](../../../docs/project-plans/developer-workbooks/non-person-identity/05-workload-identity-federation-and-managed-identities.md) links Learn rather than quoting the pages.

**How it stays honest.**

- `snapshot.json` records the upstream repository, paths, commit, dates, licenses and the size and SHA-256 of every file here. Each file's git blob hash was checked against the upstream tree at that commit before the manifest was written. `scripts/tests/test_third_party_snapshots.py` fails if any file is changed, added or removed.
- The weekly source watch follows commits to each upstream file (`entra-wif-create-trust-app-commits`, `entra-wif-create-trust-uami-commits` and `entra-wif-considerations-include-commits` in `data/source-watch/feeds.json`) and reports each one in its issue under DW (developer workbooks).
- To move to a newer upstream commit: review the upstream change, copy the files from that commit, regenerate `snapshot.json`, rerun `examples/non-person-identity/tests/NpiFederationSamples.Tests.ps1` and the Chapter 05 labs, and open a pull request. Never edit the files here; changes the program needs go in `examples/non-person-identity`.

These files keep their upstream bytes, line endings included, so the hashes match the upstream commit.
